comparisons.peer_summary: Total revenue for 2024 increased 62% compared to 2023, driven by a 60% increase in DRAM sales (due to mid-40% bit shipment growth and low-teen ASP growth) and a 72% increase in NAND sales (due to low-30% bit shipment growth and low-30% ASP growth).
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and MU disclose specific drivers for their respective revenue increases in fiscal 2024. QCOM attributes its QTL licensing revenue increase to a $402 million rise in estimated sales of multimode products, alongside decreases in unit price ($90 million) and upfront fees ($68 million). Similarly, MU attributes its total revenue increase to growth in both unit shipments (bit shipments) and average selling prices (ASP) for its DRAM and NAND products. Both disclosures break down the revenue variance into volume (sales/shipments) and price components, though QCOM notes a price decline offsetting volume growth while MU reports price growth alongside volume growth.
